title: AI products, from customer pain to shipped value.
subtitle: Each one framed the same way: customer pain → product bet → why AI (or why not) → the trade-off I made → how it was validated. Click a card to open the full case.

overview.title: From customer pain to shipped AI product

products.name: AI Policy Foundry
products.tagline: Autonomous cloud-security policy from live threat intel and your own risk register.
products.summary: Autonomous cloud-security policy generation, grounded in the organisation's own risk register — audit-ready in minutes, not weeks.
products.pain: Cloud security policy is written by hand — 2–6 weeks per policy, 60–75% coverage. Providers ship new services faster than policy keeps up, so gaps (and risk) accumulate.
products.bet: A multi-agent system that generates, validates and continuously updates policy from live threat intel **and** the organisation's own uploaded risk/control docs.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Inputs are unstructured (threat feeds, regulations, risk registers) and the mapping is non-deterministic — a language + reasoning task templating can't do. Context grounding lifts accuracy from ~65% to ~95%.
products.tradeoff: Deprioritised multi-cloud breadth to first nail per-clause traceability — an auditor won't trust a policy they can't trace back to a specific control.
products.validated: BP's cloud-security policy-management team. Their weeks-long manual cycles and creeping coverage gaps drove risk-register grounding + continuous auto-update.
outcomes: ~70% faster, ~94% coverage (modelled)
Fewer policy gaps → lower breach exposure
Roadmap: threat correlation, batch docs, OCR
products.note: Figures modelled on the public build; production figures under NDA.

products.name: AI SOC Portal
products.tagline: Auditable, AI-native SOC triage and threat hunting — every verdict replayable.
products.summary: An AI-native SOC workspace where every machine verdict can be traced, evaluated and audited — trust as a product requirement.
products.pain: Most “AI for SOC” just wires an LLM to the alert queue. But a Tier-1 analyst won't act on a verdict they can't interrogate, and a CISO won't sign off on a control they can't evidence. Trust — not capability — blocks adoption.
products.bet: Agentic triage, threat hunting and incident response over live telemetry, built so every conclusion is replayable. ~Half the repo is reasoning, evaluation and audit infrastructure.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Yes for triage, correlation and natural-language hunting (LLM + RAG excel here) — but only when paired with an explainability, evaluation and audit layer. Raw AI alone is a non-starter in a regulated SOC.
products.tradeoff: Spent the build on trust infrastructure over more raw detection features — in a regulated SOC, trust is what gates adoption.
products.validated: Multiple interview rounds across all levels of BP's SOC team. Analysts won't act on a verdict they can't interrogate — so ~half the build is eval, explainability and audit.
outcomes: Unlocks AI exactly where trust gates adoption
Faster triage; defensible, replayable verdicts
Roadmap: publish RAGAS baselines; SIEM/EDR ingest

products.name: AI Security Posture Management (AI-SPM)
products.tagline: Posture management for your own AI/ML assets, drift and compliance evidence.
products.summary: Govern and secure the organisation's own AI/ML assets across their entire lifecycle — deliberately with applied ML, not an LLM.
products.pain: Enterprises ship AI into production, but models, datasets, pipelines and endpoints are an unmanaged attack surface — no inventory, no adversarial detection, no drift monitoring — under rising NIST AI RMF / EU AI Act / GDPR pressure.
products.bet: Posture management for AI itself: inventory + lineage, adversarial-attack detection, data-quality & drift monitoring, and automated compliance evidence — one governed view for analyst, ML engineer, compliance and CISO.
products.why: Adversarial (FGSM/PGD/C&W), drift (KS, Chi-sq, Wasserstein) and anomaly (Isolation Forest/LOF/DBSCAN) problems are statistical, so the tooling is — judgment over hype.
products.tradeoff: Chose applied ML/statistics over an LLM — an LLM would add cost and risk, not accuracy.
products.validated: BP's cloud-security team on how they plan to secure the org's AI initiatives. The absence of any AI-asset inventory scoped this to posture management for AI itself.
outcomes: Makes AI adoption governable & auditable
Automated compliance evidence, Wiz-native
Roadmap: broader frameworks & integrations

products.name: Exploit Validation & Remediation MCP Server
products.tagline: A governed MCP server for the validate → approve → remediate loop.
products.summary: A governed MCP bridge that lets AI agents run the validate → approve → remediate → re-verify loop — human-in-the-loop gated.
products.pain: Vulnerability management is a broken loop: an alert fires, but proving the CVE is exploitable, getting approval, patching and re-verifying happens manually across tools — and no one dares let AI touch remediation without guardrails.
products.bet: An industry-standard MCP server so a conversational AI can safely drive a closed-loop workflow — a new consumption channel that meets engineers in their chat and IDE.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: AI owns the natural-language front door and orchestration — turning “verify this CVE and patch if real” into safe, stateful tool calls. Validation & remediation stay deterministic; approval stays human. AI orchestrates, it doesn't decide.
products.tradeoff: Kept validation and remediation deterministic and gated approval to a human — deprioritised full autonomy so security teams can actually adopt it.
products.validated: Direct Qualys customer feedback asking to stay flexible across their own and 3rd-party tooling — which drove an open, standard MCP design over a closed, one-off integration.
outcomes: Extends the risk platform to safe AI agents
Cuts mean-time-to-remediate
Roadmap: live-API mode, deeper autonomy matrix

products.name: Unified Risk Copilot
products.tagline: Conversational risk triage across 8 security modules, fully audited.
products.summary: One conversation that joins 8 security modules into a ranked, evidence-backed, auditable remediation plan.
products.pain: Teams run 8+ modules (VM, WAS, PC, TotalCloud, Container, Cloud Agent, Patch, CSAM) in separate UIs. No single “what to fix first” view, the CISO's weekly report is a manual spreadsheet, and managers want data without write access.
products.bet: A “Weekly Risk Copilot” on the official MCP server: an LLM joins all 8 modules into one ranked narrative — with allow-listing, read-only mode, audit logging and approval-gated remediation baked in.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Cross-domain correlation, NL querying and report synthesis are the LLM sweet spot — the join logic is fuzzy and the output is prose. Governance is deterministic guardrails; remediation is human-approved.
products.tradeoff: Shipped read-only + approval-gated first — deprioritised write/automation to earn trust before letting AI act across 8 modules.
products.validated: The same Qualys customer signal — stay flexible across the stack — led to wrapping the official MCP server, not building yet another siloed console.
outcomes: Weekly risk report: hours → minutes
Defensible, fully audited, safe self-service
Roadmap: live qualys-cli, more agent actions

products.name: HS Code Prediction API
products.tagline: Customs classification with right-sized classic ML — not an LLM.
products.summary: Automating customs classification from a plain-text product description — classic ML, right-sized, not an LLM.
products.pain: Customs classification (assigning HS codes) is manual, slow and error-prone. A wrong code means fines, shipment delays and compliance risk — and trade teams still look codes up by hand, item by item.
products.bet: A production-shaped microservice that predicts an HS code — with chapter / heading / subheading breakdown and confidence — from free text. Drops into a trade pipeline as a cheap-to-serve API.
products.why: A canonical supervised text-classification task — so classic ML (TF-IDF + logistic regression). Lightweight, explainable and cheap: matching model complexity to the problem is itself the product decision.
products.tradeoff: Shipped classic ML at ~55% rather than chase an LLM — a cheap, explainable, deployable pipeline beat SOTA accuracy for this buyer's need.
products.validated: eBay's need to show an accurate total landed cost at checkout; validated with customs domain experts on how HS codes are really assigned.
outcomes: Accurate landed cost at checkout; less manual work
Ship-ready, cheap-to-serve ML packaging
Roadmap: transformer models, batch predict, caching

products.name: KYC-as-a-Service
products.tagline: Verifiable, privacy-preserving credit scoring — AI on a blockchain.
products.summary: Verifiable, privacy-preserving credit-risk scoring — AI wrapped in blockchain provenance and federated learning.
products.pain: Banks need real-time, auditable credit-risk scores, but AI scoring is a black box regulators distrust — and institutions can't pool data to improve models without exposing customer PII.
products.bet: A three-layer hybrid: blockchain as immutable source-of-truth & model provenance, off-chain AI for scoring, and a signed API — plus federated learning so institutions improve the model without sharing raw data.
products.why: Credit scoring on tabular/behavioural features is supervised ML, so GBM, not an LLM. The real innovation is wrapping AI in verifiability and privacy — the barriers, not the maths.
products.tradeoff: Invested in verifiability (blockchain) and privacy (federated learning) over model sophistication — those were the real barriers to adoption.
products.validated: Western Union customers couldn't get credit in a new country without history or documents; KYC requirements validated with multiple financial institutions.
outcomes: Adoptable AI scoring for regulated finance
Multi-institution collaboration, GDPR-aware
Solves thin-file cold-start via shared learning

ecosystem.title: The AI Defence Ecosystem.
ecosystem.subtitle: Three products, one platform, the full lifecycle — because AI both defends the enterprise and becomes something the enterprise must defend.

pillars.name: AI Policy Foundry
pillars.text: Generate & maintain cloud-security policy from live intel + the org's risk register.

pillars.name: AI-SPM
pillars.text: Govern the org's own AI/ML assets — adversarial defence, drift, compliance evidence.

pillars.name: AI SOC Portal
pillars.text: Auditable, AI-native triage, hunting & response over live security telemetry.

ecosystem.spine: **One trust spine across all three** — every AI decision is explainable, evaluated and logged. Gaps found in Detect feed back to Prevent; assets in Protect are watched by Detect.
opportunity: AI-security spend is surging but fragmented into point tools — no one owns the whole lifecycle.
Regulation (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) is forcing every enterprise to govern its AI — a mandatory, expanding buyer need.
“AI as defender” and “AI as attack surface” treated as one problem — a category few competitors frame this way.
differentiator: Full-lifecycle coverage — prevent → protect → detect & respond — vs. single-point competitors.
Trust as a first-class product layer, grounded in the customer's own risk register and AI assets.
Governed, human-in-the-loop agentic action — never an autonomous black box. Land in one pillar, expand across the loop.
